title: Pronounce Button and Streaming Playback
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Text-to-Speech
Audio Streaming Playback
Pronounce Button
Intelligent Textbook Media
description: Three glossary terms each have a pronounce button. Selecting one starts a timing simulation with two progress bars for the same audio clip: streaming playback, where the playback position starts moving as soon as the first part of the file arrives, and download-first, where nothing plays until the whole file has arrived. Each bar shows a Downloaded marker, a Playback Position marker, and its time to first sound. A checkbox simulates a slow connection. No sound is played; all timings are example values.

learningObjectives: Demonstrate how clicking a pronounce button begins audio streaming playback before the full narration has loaded.
Compare the time to first sound for streaming playback and for waiting for a full download.
Explain why the playback position can never pass the downloaded marker.
prerequisites: Has read the definitions of text-to-speech narration, audio streaming playback, and pronounce button
Knows that a file takes time to download

simulation.modelType: Timing model of download and playback
equations: downloaded(t) = min(clip length, first chunk + (t - start delay) x download rate)
streaming playback advances at 1 second per second and never passes downloaded(t)
download-first playback starts when downloaded(t) equals the clip length
assumptions: The clip is 4 seconds long and the first chunk holds 0.25 seconds of audio
Normal connection: 0.2 second start delay, 4.0 seconds of audio received per second
Slow connection: 0.6 second start delay, 0.8 seconds of audio received per second
A stalled streaming player resumes once 0.4 seconds of audio is buffered
limitations: No sound is played and nothing is downloaded
All timings are example values, not measurements of any text-to-speech service
Does not model variable network speed

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: The learner triggers playback and compares two delivery methods on the same clip, then changes the connection speed and compares again
keyQuestions: When does the listener hear the first sound on each timeline?
Why can the playback position never pass the downloaded marker?
commonMisconceptions: Streaming makes the audio file download faster
A player can play parts of a file that have not arrived yet
assessmentOpportunities: Predict which time to first sound changes more on a slow connection, then test the prediction
